evals.prompt: The PM has approved the onboarding spec for Basil. The onboarding flow uses the real AI layer (basil-chat-api) from the user's first message, with an extraction step running after each user message. Review the spec for security and cost requirements before the Architect writes the TDD.
evals.expected_output: Must identify: (1) Authentication — onboarding endpoint must require a valid Supabase session; unauthenticated requests must return 401 before reaching the AI layer; (2) Rate limiting — onboarding makes multiple AI calls per session; must define a per-user limit (e.g. max 10 AI calls during onboarding) enforced server-side; (3) AI cost exposure — calculate worst-case cost per onboarding session (input tokens for system prompt + user messages + extraction calls); flag if unbounded conversation could result in high cost per user; recommend a max-turns limit for the onboarding session; (4) Input sanitisation — user input reaches the AI layer; must be length-capped server-side (e.g. 2000 chars max per message); (5) Extraction call cost — the extraction step is a second AI call per user message; must be factored into rate limit and cost calculations; (6) PHI posture — user's first message may contain sensitive personal content; confirm Sentry scrubbing applies to onboarding endpoints; (7) No paywall concern for onboarding specifically — but confirm that the onboarding endpoint is separate from the paid-tier chat endpoint so rate limits can be set independently. Must deliver findings as a list of named requirements for the Architect to include in the TDD — not as prose concerns.

evals.prompt: Basil's paid tier (Basil Care) includes unlimited conversation and persistent memory. The free tier has a limited message cap. Review the paywall design for security gaps before the Architect writes the subscription TDD.
evals.expected_output: Must identify: (1) API-layer enforcement — the message cap and feature gate must be checked server-side on every request; a UI-only gate is not a gate; must name the specific check (e.g. query user's subscription tier from Supabase before processing AI call); (2) Token spoofing — confirm the subscription tier is read from a server-side source (Supabase row, RevenueCat webhook) not from a client-supplied value in the request body; (3) Free tier abuse — a free-tier user must not be able to reach paid-tier endpoints by modifying request headers or body; (4) Rate limiting on free tier — free tier must have a hard server-side cap with a clear 429 response and a user-facing message; (5) Cost ceiling — calculate worst-case cost if every free-tier user maxes out their cap on a single day; confirm this is acceptable before the cap is set; (6) Subscription state race condition — if a user's subscription lapses mid-session, define what happens to in-flight AI calls; (7) Webhook security — if RevenueCat webhooks are used to update subscription state, the webhook endpoint must verify the signature before updating any user record. Must flag any of these that are missing from the spec as explicit TDD requirements.
